gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AeroClip 2's 8 h rating is measured with AAC at 50% volume and drops to 5 h with LDAC on (3 h at 100%), which is less than the C50i's 7 h. Soundcore's own C50i FAQ also lists LDAC (SBC/AAC/LDAC) and says dual connection is off while LDAC is on, so LDAC does not set the AeroClip 2 apart.
standout_why: Compared against the cited soundcore.com AeroClip 2 and C50i product pages (8H/32H vs 7H/28H, no codec or volume conditions, no LDAC battery figure), the uncited Soundcore 'AeroClip vs AeroClip 2' blog (music 8h/32h and call 5h/20h, no LDAC figure, does not list LDAC for AeroClip 2), SoundGuys' C50i page and HearWiki (both list LDAC for C50i but give no LDAC battery hit or multipoint restriction), and our own current page (lists LDAC only on the AeroClip 2). None gives the AeroClip 2's LDAC playtime or the C50i's LDAC/multipoint lockout. The C50i's LDAC support is partly covered by SoundGuys and HearWiki, but no page ChatGPT cited has it, and all three ChatGPT answers present LDAC as an AeroClip 2 advantage. The B&H compare page returned 403, so it was not checked.
decides: This confirms the C50i as the pick for music and everyday use and narrows the AeroClip 2 case to calls only. Both ChatGPT answers that give winners credit the AeroClip 2 for music partly because of LDAC, and the table one gives it a 'modest' battery win. Soundcore's own figures say the C50i also does LDAC. With LDAC on, the AeroClip 2 runs 5 h at 50% volume against the C50i's 7 h (the C50i figure is at Soundcore's standard test codec, not LDAC). In call mode, the gap is 5 h (AeroClip 2) vs 4.5 h (C50i). The AeroClip 2's real edge stays the 4 mics + 2 VPU call pickup and the 10 min = 4 h fast charge (vs 2 h). That is what the $100 gap at list price ($169.99 vs $69.99 on us.soundcore.com) pays for.
